description: Environmental Humanities is the name given to the effort to bring together the humanities (literature, art, history, philosophy) and the sciences to address contemporary environmental problems like climate change. This approach recognizes the physical, cultural, and social elements that contribute to complex definitions of environment and environmental problems. In this seminar, we will explore a variety of texts that engage the sciences and humanities to appreciate the essential role that storytelling, poetry, cinema, and other creative genres play in bringing diverse voices and multicultural perspectives to understanding and addressing environmental issues. Students will write a narrative argument, critical analysis, and develop a research project based on a course theme or subject.
